reference.source: Zuikaku as at Leyte Gulf, October 1944, drawn from KTKloss's Shokaku (the sisters share a hull; Track M, M1e, Mark 2026-10-09). lengthM (257.5 m / 844 ft 10 in overall), flightDeck.lengthM and widthM (242.2 m / 794 ft 7 in, 29 m / 95 ft 2 in maximum width) and the ten transverse arrestor wires from the English Wikipedia article 'Shokaku-class aircraft carrier', read 2026-10-09; maxSpeedMps is its 34.5 kn designed speed. deckWidthM is the flight deck's 29 m. beamM (26 m) is an ESTIMATE of the waterline beam: the article gives only the 29 m overall beam. flightDeck.heightM and deckHeightM are the SAME ESTIMATE, the model's own flight deck (15.5 m / 51 ft above the waterline once fitted to 257.5 m); no freeboard figure was found. trapZone is an ESTIMATE laid over the ten wires aft, scaled from essex-cv's. paddles, turnRateRadPerS and hullHp are essex-cv's, so the two carriers play alike: CHOICES, not history. ARMAMENT, CHOSEN FOR BALANCE AGAINST essex-cv (M1d D3), NOT HISTORY: the eight twin 12.7 cm Type 89 dual-purpose mounts are real (two pairs a side on the hull sponsons, as on the mesh; generated kits) and carried as turrets with aa: heavy, as essex-cv carries its 5-inch. Light AA is four triple 25 mm Type 96 mounts, two a side, in the deck-edge gallery tubs nearest the island and aft. The real 1944 fit after the Philippine Sea was 20 triple and 36 single 25 mm (96 barrels) and eight 28-round 12 cm AA rocket launchers (same article, Armament, citing Lengerer and Campbell). The model's own 25 mm guns and 12.7 cm mounts are removed (its entry's Drop splits); its other gallery tubs stand empty.
